subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A foundational tour of CS, ordered in three chapters: foundations, building the system, and optimisation & systems.

courses.name: Chapter 1, Foundations
courses.description: Where it all starts: what computer science studies, how to express ideas as code, and how to write simple algorithms.

topics.name: Introduction to Computer Science
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on Computer Science (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: Computer science is most accurately described as the study of:
options: Computers, and how to build them physically

questions.prompt: What base does the binary number system use?
How many bits are in one byte?
What does a CPU primarily do?
options: Stores files long-term on a disk
Fetches and executes instructions encoded in memory
Connects the computer to the network

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler runs faster than an interpreter at compile time
An interpreter produces a binary file; a compiler does not
A compiler translates the whole program to machine code ahead of time; an interpreter executes source line-by-line at runtime
Compilers can only handle Python; interpreters can only handle C

topics.name: Programming Fundamentals
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on programming languages (CC BY-SA 4.0) and the Python documentation (PSF License).

questions.prompt: What is the role of a comment in code?
options: It is executed before any other line
It is ignored by the compiler/interpreter and used to explain code to humans
It compiles to a faster binary

questions.prompt: Which of these is Python's standard execution model?
options: Ahead-of-time compiled to native machine code
Interpreted (compiled to bytecode that the Python virtual machine then runs)

questions.prompt: What does a high-level language abstract away compared to assembly?
options: Direct manipulation of CPU registers and memory addresses

questions.prompt: In Python, how are blocks of code grouped?
Which is true about an expression versus a statement?
options: An expression evaluates to a value; a statement performs an action
Statements always return a value; expressions never do
Only statements can be assigned to variables

topics.name: Variables & Control Flow
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on control flow (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: What is a variable in programming?
options: A named reference to a value stored in memory
A line of code that runs only once
A reserved keyword that cannot change

questions.prompt: What does an if/else statement express?
options: A repetition of the same code many times
A branching choice: run one block of code when a condition is true, another when false
A definition of a new function
An import of an external library

questions.prompt: When would you prefer a for loop over a while loop?
options: When you don't know how many iterations are needed in advance
When you want the loop to run forever
When iterating over a known sequence or a fixed range of values

questions.prompt: What does the break statement do inside a loop?
options: Pauses the program and waits for input
Exits the innermost enclosing loop immediately

questions.prompt: Which is true about variable scope?
options: All variables are global by default in every language
Scope is the region of code where a variable is accessible, typically a function or block
Scope is the variable's data type
Scope refers to how much memory the variable consumes

topics.name: Basic Algorithms
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on algorithms (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: What is an algorithm?
options: A finite, ordered sequence of well-defined instructions that solves a problem or computes a result
A hardware component inside a CPU

questions.prompt: Which operation describes filtering a list?
options: Removing elements that don't satisfy a given condition
Sorting the list in ascending order

questions.prompt: To find the maximum value in an unsorted list of n elements, you must compare:
What is pseudocode used for?
options: Describing the steps of an algorithm in plain, language-independent terms before writing real code
Compressing code to take less disk space
Hiding the algorithm from other developers

questions.prompt: Why do we measure algorithm efficiency?
options: Because every algorithm always behaves the same on every input
Because runtime and memory matter when input sizes grow, and different algorithms scale very differently
Only academic researchers care about this

courses.name: Chapter 2, Building the System
courses.description: From structured code to the maths and hardware that underpin it.

topics.name: Object-Oriented Programming
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on object-oriented programming (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: What is a class in object-oriented programming?
options: A blueprint that defines the data and behaviour of a kind of object

questions.prompt: An object is best described as:
options: A specific instance of a class, with its own state

questions.prompt: What does inheritance allow you to do?
options: Run two programs at the same time
Define a new class that reuses and extends the behaviour of an existing class

questions.prompt: Encapsulation is the OOP principle that:
options: Forces all classes to be defined in the same file
Bundles data with the methods that operate on it, and hides internal details from the outside
Requires every method to be public

questions.prompt: Polymorphism means that:
options: Each class can only have one method
Objects of different classes can be used through a shared interface, with the right behaviour selected at runtime
A program can be written in multiple languages
Memory addresses change every time the program runs

topics.name: Data Structures
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on data structures (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of accessing an element of an array by index?
Which abstract data type follows Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) order?
Which abstract data type follows First-In-First-Out (FIFO) order?
Why might you choose a linked list over an array?
options: O(1) insertion or deletion at known positions, without reallocating storage

questions.prompt: What is the worst-case time complexity of inserting into the middle of a singly linked list, given only a pointer to its head?

topics.name: Discrete Mathematics
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on discrete mathematics (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: A set in mathematics is best described as:
options: An ordered list of values, with duplicates allowed
A collection of distinct objects, with no notion of order
A function that maps inputs to outputs

questions.prompt: The union of sets A and B is:
options: The set of elements that are in both A and B
The set of elements that are in either A or B (or both)
The set of elements in A but not in B

questions.prompt: What does the expression n! (n factorial) compute?
options: The product of all positive integers from 1 to n
The number of bits required to store n

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a permutation and a combination?
options: Permutations and combinations are the same
A permutation cares about the order of selection; a combination does not
A combination is always larger than a permutation
A permutation can only be of 2 elements

questions.prompt: In graph theory, a graph consists of:
options: A set of vertices (nodes) and a set of edges connecting pairs of vertices

topics.name: Computer Organization & Architecture
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on computer architecture (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: What does a logic gate do?
options: Stores data permanently on a disk
Implements a simple boolean operation on one or more input signals to produce an output signal
Connects the computer to a network

questions.prompt: An AND gate outputs 1 (true) when:
What is the role of the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit)?
options: Perform arithmetic and bitwise logical operations on register values

questions.prompt: Which memory tier is fastest to access?
A CPU clock cycle is:
options: The total time to run a program
The smallest unit of time over which the CPU advances state, set by the clock frequency
The time taken to boot the operating system
How long the screen stays on between refreshes

courses.name: Chapter 3, Optimisation & Systems
courses.description: Making things fast, persistent, scheduled, and connected, algorithm analysis, databases, operating systems, networks.

topics.name: Design & Analysis of Algorithms
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on algorithm analysis (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: Big O notation expresses:
options: How an algorithm's running time or memory grows as the input size grows, in the worst case
The memory address of a program

questions.prompt: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search through an unsorted array of n elements?
Binary search requires the input array to be:
Which sorting algorithm has an average-case time complexity of O(n log n)?
A space–time trade-off in algorithm design means:
options: You can often reduce running time by using more memory (e.g. caching), or vice versa
Algorithms always run in constant space
Algorithms run faster when given less memory

topics.name: Database Management Systems
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on database systems (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: What does SQL stand for?
Which SQL statement reads data from a table?
What is a primary key?
options: The first column of a table
A column (or set of columns) whose value uniquely identifies each row in a table
The largest value in the table
The administrator's password for the database

questions.prompt: What does a JOIN clause do?
options: Combines rows from two or more tables based on a related column
Adds a new column to a table

questions.prompt: The goal of database normalisation is to:
options: Eliminate redundant data and reduce update anomalies by structuring tables according to a set of rules (normal forms)
Increase the size of the database on disk

topics.name: Operating Systems
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on operating systems (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: What is a process?
options: An instance of a program in execution, with its own memory space

questions.prompt: RAM and disk storage differ primarily in that:
options: RAM is much slower than disk
RAM is volatile (its contents are lost on power-off) and much faster to access than disk
Disk is volatile; RAM is permanent

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between a process and a thread?
options: Threads run on a separate computer; processes run locally
A process has its own memory space; threads within a process share memory
Threads can only do I/O; processes can only do computation

questions.prompt: What problem does virtual memory solve?
options: It speeds up the CPU clock
It lets processes use more memory than is physically available by paging chunks to disk, and isolates each process's address space
It encrypts data on the hard drive

questions.prompt: A deadlock occurs when:
options: A process runs out of CPU time
Two or more processes are each waiting forever for a resource the other holds

topics.name: Computer Networks
topics.attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia articles on computer networking (CC BY-SA 4.0).

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an IP address?
options: It is the user's password on a website
It uniquely identifies a network interface on a network so packets can be routed to it
It is the brand of the network card

questions.prompt: What does TCP guarantee that UDP does not?
options: Reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of a byte stream

questions.prompt: What does DNS do?
options: Translates domain names like example.com into IP addresses
Compresses web pages before sending them

questions.prompt: HTTP is a protocol that sits on top of which transport-layer protocol by default?
Which scenario is UDP a better fit for than TCP?
options: Transferring a large file where every byte must arrive intact
Sending an HTTP request to a web server
Real-time video or voice, where late packets are useless and dropping a few is acceptable
Logging in to a remote shell
